correctness.rationale: For each as-yet-unseen label, conditional incoming probability is exactly 1/m, independently of adaptive outgoing choice, and no outgoing label may be globally unseen. Hence the uncovered-set Markov transition kernel equals iid sampling with replacement on the m initially absent labels; geometric waiting times yield mean, variance, and inclusion-exclusion CDF. In the iid packet model, the hypergeometric novelty has mean rk/n; the (n/r)H_k potential has expected descent at least one and strictly greater at the initial stage if r,m>=2. Boundary cases r=1,m=1 are exact. 2747 exact standard-library assertions passed; finite checks do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary Conjecture 2.4 concerns the dependent s-subset coupon collector, proves r=s, and predicts only an asymptotic s=1 mean. Its independent-packet results and a broad 2016 iid study do not imply the policy-invariant exact s=1 law nor the sharp finite all-(n,r) sign reversal. Actual indexed-literature and accessible historical-claim searches found no equivalent all-parameter statement. The older Adler–Ross iid formula is explicitly treated as prior; unidentified general coupon bounds remain residual historical risks.

value.rationale: The work supplies an exact distributional solution of the natural single-coupon specialization of the 2023 dependent-subset cover-time question, robust even under nonanticipating adaptive departures. The same theorem establishes a sharp strict finite n,r boundary contrasting dependent replacement versus independent packets, with reversal in the r=1 and n-r=1 families despite large-n slowdown. The complete threshold is motivated by the original comparison, not an arbitrary parameter slice or numeric improvement.
